issues.legal_issue: Expenditure incurred wholly and exclusively for an indivisible business is deductible in full even when part of the business income is not taxable.
material_facts: The assessee’s cultivation of sugar cane and manufacture of sugar were found to constitute one single and indivisible business.
The assessee paid its managing agents commission for managing the business and claimed the commission as a business expense.
The commission was incurred wholly and exclusively for the business, although income arising from the cultivation activity was not taxable.
issues.conclusion: The entire managing agency commission was deductible; the fact that part of the income from the business was not taxable was irrelevant.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(xv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, expenditure laid out or expended wholly and exclusively for the purpose of the business is deductible. The court must apply the statutory language, not equitable considerations, and need not trace otherwise deductible business expenditure to taxable income. The court followed C.I.T., Bombay v. Parakh and (India) Ltd. and C.I.T., Madras v. Indian Bank Ltd.; it also referred to S.A.S.S. Chellappa Chettiar v. C.I.T., Madras and Salt & Industries Agencies Ltd. v. C.I.T., Bombay City.

rule.if: business_tax_deduction_assessment and indivisible_business and expense_wholly_for_business and part_business_income_not_taxable

predicates.business_tax_deduction_assessment: The case concerns a claim to deduct a business expense in a tax assessment.
predicates.indivisible_business: The business activities giving rise to taxable and non-taxable income form one single and indivisible business.
predicates.expense_wholly_for_business: The taxpayer incurred the claimed expense wholly and exclusively for the purpose of that business.
predicates.part_business_income_not_taxable: Some income arising from the business is not taxable.

issues.definition: When a tax assessment concerns an expense incurred wholly for one indivisible business, the expense is deductible in full even if part of that business’s income is not taxable.

issues.legal_issue: The restriction on deducting expenditure incurred as a cultivator does not apply to managing agency commission that is a general business expense rather than expenditure on cultivation operations.
material_facts: The assessee’s cultivation and sugar manufacture formed one business, and agricultural produce was used in the manufacturing business.
The disputed expenditure was commission paid to managing agents for managing the assessee’s business.
The commission was not expenditure incurred by the assessee as a cultivator in raising crops or carrying out incidental and supplementary cultivation activities.
issues.conclusion: Rule 23 did not permit the Department to disallow or apportion the managing agency commission as expenditure incurred by the assessee as a cultivator.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 23 of the rules under the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, provides that, when computing taxable business income partly derived from agricultural produce, no further deduction is made for expenditure incurred as a cultivator or receiver of rent in kind. Read with section 2(1), the restriction concerns cultivation and activities incidental or supplementary to raising and preparing produce for sale; it does not cover general business disbursements such as managing agency commission.

rule.if: business_tax_deduction_assessment and mixed_agricultural_business_income and managing_agency_commission and not cultivation_operation_expense

predicates.business_tax_deduction_assessment: The case concerns the computation of taxable business income in a tax assessment.
predicates.mixed_agricultural_business_income: The business income includes income connected with agricultural produce used in the business, alongside income chargeable to tax.
predicates.managing_agency_commission: The taxpayer paid commission to agents for managing the business.
predicates.cultivation_operation_expense: The disputed expense was incurred by the taxpayer in raising crops or in activities incidental or supplementary to cultivation and preparing the produce for sale.

issues.definition: In a tax assessment involving agricultural and business income, managing agency commission is outside the cultivator-expense restriction when it is not expenditure on cultivation operations.
